title: Pocket Draft Duel
user: Two to four friends who want a 15-minute tactical card-game session by room code, with a new fair draft each run and no collection, login, or deck building beforehand.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Discussion of The Deck says a compelling digital game-night use case is letting people create and share their own game rules, while another commenter values one-host/scan-to-join setup.
The Deck is an open-source mobile turn-by-turn card-game engine, demonstrating infrastructure exists but not a focused browser game built around a fresh short-session draft.

recurrence: Game-night participants repeatedly value no-search, one-host joining and flexible rules, yet general engines leave the actual approachable game to somebody else.
current_workaround: Bring a physical deck, install a card app, or teach a longer collectible-card game.
incumbents_and_gap: The Deck, Board Game Arena, and Codenames-style sites support particular games or engines; they do not offer a browser-native micro-draft whose preparation is the game.
smallest_useful_product: Room-code 2–4 player simultaneous draft of 18 public-domain-icon cards, then three three-minute battles with one chosen tactic per round. Non-goals: collectible cards, ranked ladder, chat, or custom-card publishing.
success_measure: 60% of completed rooms launch a rematch and median time from URL open to first pick is below two minutes.
monetization: one-time — a modest host unlock for additional balanced draft sets fits a contained game better than a recurring charge.
constraints: Use original/public-domain art only; server-authoritative simultaneous picks; do not create a gambling-like economy or paid random packs.
why_distinct: It turns the shared draft into a complete, repeatable run instead of recreating a collectible card game or generic engine.
